name: servo-connector
title: Hobby servo connector with bulk capacitor
about: A 3-pin 2.54 mm header for a hobby servo – pin 1 signal, pin 2 +5 V, pin 3 GND – and 1000 µF across +5 V and GND at the connector, which supplies the servo's start and stall current peaks close to the servo instead of through the board's supply path.

ports.sig: the servo's control signal (a PWM-capable GPIO)
ports.vservo: the servo's supply, typically 5 V (4.8–6 V servos)

components.label: {as}: servo (1 signal, 2 +, 3 GND)
components.notes: Pin 1 = signal, pin 2 = + (the middle), pin 3 = GND. Through-hole, hand-soldered at JLCPCB.

components.label: {as}: 1000 µF at the servo connector
components.notes: Electrolytic, pin 1 = plus. Directly beside J1.

notes: Pin order: assumption – the usual order of hobby-servo leads (signal, + in the middle, ground) was not read in a servo data sheet here; check the servo's. With + in the middle a plug turned round swaps only signal and ground.

The servo's current: give the load in sim.json as an external current on J1 (plus "2", minus "3") – its running current, and its stall current as a fault case ("matrix": false); maker-coverage MOT 16 names 2.5 A for an MG996R at stall (not read here). J1 carries 3 A (XFCN drawing): LIM.i holds it.

1000 µF / 16 V: design choice; the servo data sheets name no capacitor. 1 mF gives a 1 A, 1 ms current peak a sag of 1 V before the supply path takes over (ΔV = I·t / C, ESR not given). Rated ≥ 1.5 × 6 V. Ripple current 347 mA at 120 Hz (C3359): a servo's 50 Hz current pulses can exceed it – a larger or second capacitor for big servos.

Supply: a servo on the MCU's rail resets it when it starts or stalls (maker-coverage MOT 16, FT-1) – give vservo its own regulator or supply, joined at ground. USB alone gives 500 mA (HINT.usb_budget).

The signal: a GPIO directly; on a long cable a series resistor at the MCU protects the pin (HINT.cable_line). Whether a 3.3 V signal is enough for a 5 V servo, its data sheet says – none was read here.

t_servo.about: block test: a servo holding its position, 0.2 A at J2 (2 → 3), LEDs off – within the example's 0.5 A USB source
